{{Nihongo|'''Mitsutaka Fujita'''|藤田 光孝|Fujita Mitsutaka|August 16, 1959 – March 18, 1998}} was a Japanese physicist. He proposed the edge state that is unique to 
[[graphene]] zigzag edges. Also, he theoretically pointed out the importance and peculiarity of nanoscale and edge shape effects in [[nanographene]].  The theoretical concept of [[graphene nanoribbons]] was introduced by him and his research group to study the nanoscale effect of graphene. He was an associate professor at [[Tsukuba University]], and died of a [[subarachnoid hemorrhage]] on March 18, 1998. His [[posthumous name]] is {{Nihongo|Rikakuin-Shinju-Houkou-Koji|理覚院深珠放光居士}} in Japanese.

==Awards==
After his death, the original paper on graphene edge state and graphene nanoribbons was awarded the JPS Best Paper Award in March 2003 from the Physical Society of Japan.
*[https://web.archive.org/web/20091208030902/http://wwwsoc.nii.ac.jp/jps/jps/guide/ronbunsyo/ronbun8_03.html JPS Best Paper award], [[Physical Society of Japan]]
